content.user_title: Draft and Schedule Social Posts with TimeToPost
content.value_statement: Managing platform-specific posts requires consistent wording, account selection, and approval. This skill guides TimeToPost MCP drafting, timing recommendations, and scheduling after explicit user approval.
actual_capabilities: Check the TimeToPost workspace, publishing permission, supported capabilities, and connected account IDs.
Read recent account posts to match vocabulary, casing, rhythm, and typical length.
Create distinct platform-specific drafts for human review.
Request account-based posting times and label fallback suggestions as generic heuristics.
Inspect approval queues, schedule explicitly approved drafts, and check resulting status.
Prepare campaign-tagged links through an available hosted helper or the bundled offline URL helper.
limitations: Live drafting and scheduling require an authenticated TimeToPost MCP connection and connected social accounts.
Draft-only connections cannot schedule posts; each scheduling action requires approval of the exact copy, account, and time.
Account-specific timing depends on available history; bundled platform limits require live capability checks.
Media requires the documented hosting and upload flow; hosted and stdio connections may expose different tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Product Announcement
use_cases.description: Create distinct announcement drafts for connected accounts and review copy, destination accounts, and suggested times before scheduling.

use_cases.title: Review Client Approval Queues
use_cases.description: Inspect pending drafts in the intended workspace and schedule only the specific versions approved by the client.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Consistent Publishing Voice
use_cases.description: Use recent posts to prepare account-specific content while checking facts and adapting wording for each platform.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Social Accounts
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my TimeToPost workspace, connected accounts, and publishing permissions. Do not create drafts or schedule anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the connection without changing content.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Platform-Specific Announcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft separate LinkedIn and X posts about [announcement] for [audience]. Match my recent posts. Ask for missing facts and keep everything pending review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: create distinct drafts without scheduling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Weekly Review Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare three distinct posts about [topic] for [account IDs]. Suggest times in [time zone] using available history. Show every draft without scheduling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review multiple drafts and proposed times.

prompt_templates.title: Schedule an Explicitly Approved Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Show draft [draft ID], its exact copy, account ID, and proposed time in [time zone]. Wait for my explicit confirmation before scheduling. Then verify status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: confirm a specific scheduling action and check the result.

output_examples.input: Draft separate LinkedIn and X announcements for our new Monday community workshop. Keep both pending review.
output: LinkedIn draft: Our community workshop starts Monday. What would you like us to cover in the first session?
X draft: New community workshop starts Monday. Which topic should we explore first?
Review status: Both versions remain pending approval. Nothing is scheduled.

output_examples.input: Suggest a time for my draft when no account history is available. Use America/Los_Angeles.
output: Timing basis: No account-specific recommendation is available.
Proposed time: Tuesday at noon, America/Los_Angeles. This is a generic heuristic, not an account-based result.
Approval status: Scheduling awaits your approval of the exact draft, account, and time.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, publishing permission, and connected account IDs before creating or approving drafts.
Review exact copy, destination accounts, time zone, and proposed times before authorizing scheduling.
Check current platform capabilities and review campaign attribution before using tagged links.
anti_patterns: Scheduling a draft based on implied approval or approval of an earlier version.
Posting identical text across platforms or inventing unsupported product claims.
Treating generic timing suggestions or bundled platform limits as verified account-specific information.

faq.question: Do I need a TimeToPost account?
faq.answer: Yes. Live operations require an authenticated TimeToPost MCP connection. Social accounts must be connected before they can receive posts.

faq.question: Does creating a draft publish it?
faq.answer: No. Draft creation produces pending approval items. Approving a draft schedules it, so the workflow requires explicit approval first.

faq.question: Can a draft-only connection schedule posts?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare drafts, but scheduling depends on publishing permission reported by the service.

faq.question: How are posting times selected?
faq.answer: The workflow requests account-based recommendations first. Without history, it labels suggested times as generic heuristics and asks for the time zone.

faq.question: Where should I provide authentication credentials?
faq.answer: Use the hosted OAuth flow when supported. For stdio setup, inject your token through a local environment variable, not chat or committed configuration.

faq.question: Are campaign link tools available on every connection?
faq.answer: No. The hosted helper may be unavailable on stdio connections. A bundled offline URL helper is provided; review attribution before using it.
